Sam: ran a bunch of nsys sweeps on the new kernel-selection heuristic (seq_threshold=32 -> choose_small_seq_kernels). seeing a perf regression and a big drop in KV cache hit rate. dumping minimal logs + timeline snippets below, can someone eyeball? :eyes:

Sam: nsys summary (condensed):
```
Total GPU time: 1200 ms
kernel: matmul_large            30%   360 ms
kernel: attention_small_seq     25%   300 ms
kernel: kv_lookup               12%   144 ms
KV cache hits: 42 / 100 tokens (42%)   <-- used to be ~92% on baseline
prefix reuse: heatmap shows churn in first 8 tokens
# tail latency jumped (p99 went from ~68ms -> ~160ms)
```

Elaine: can you attach the full nsys timeline? suspect kernel boundaries changed and we might be breaking same-stream semantics for prefix ops. small-seq kernels often get routed differently which can fragment KV cache keys.

Sam: pasted a small nvtx timeline slice (timestamps are relative):
```
[0ms] dispatch: request A (seq_len 12)
[2ms] kernel: attention_small_seq (stream 3)
[5ms] kernel: kv_lookup_prefix (stream 5)  <-- different stream id
8ms: kernel: write_kv_cache (stream 5)
12ms: kernel: attention_small_seq (stream 3)
```
Notice write/read across different streams for same request. not sure if that alone causes evictions but it's suspicious.

Mike: stream juggling can definitely affect ordering + LRU windows for our cache implementation. if write_kv_cache executes later on another stream it may race with other requests and cause early evictions. can you dump kv eviction logs with timestamps?

Sam: quick grep from runtime logs:
```
KVCache: store key=0x7fffa21b, seq_start=0, seq_end=63, stream=5, store_ts=1612345678901
KVCache: evict key=0x7fffa21b, reason=capacity, evict_ts=1612345678908, victim_key=0x7fff9c10
KVCache: lookup key=0x7fffa21b -> MISS (was evicted)
```
Pattern: store then shortly after evict. before the heuristic change saves same key across requests (no eviction).

Javier: can you run nvprof to get per-kernel occupancy and active warps? sometimes the small-seq kernel path uses kernels compiled with different block sizes which reduces occupancy and increases per-token time; that plus more kernels increases pressure on the cache window. try: `nvprof --print-gpu-trace --profile-from-start off --metrics gld_transactions` on a short workload.

perf-bot: automatic trace upload: https://artifacts.example/company/traces/1812345678/ (nsys + perfetto combined). summary attached: KV_hit_rate=0.42, avg_kernel_count_per_token=4.1, avg_kernel_count_before=1.8.

Elaine: hypothesis: kernel selection split creates additional kernel launches per token which increases interleaving across requests -> KV entries are less likely to be hot when looked up. also check that the cache key includes the stream id or any ephemeral run-id; if key encoding accidentally includes launch-order-dependent bits, you'll never hit.

Mike: quick local reproduction script I ran:
```
# run baseline vs new heuristic (short workload)
python tools/run_profile.py --model small --seqs 10,12,16 --heuristic baseline > baseline.log
python tools/run_profile.py --model small --seqs 10,12,16 --heuristic choose_small_seq_kernels > new.log
# then parse
scripts/kv-stats.py baseline.log new.log
```
baseline -> KV hits 92% p50 28ms p99 68ms
new -> KV hits 42% p50 32ms p99 160ms

Sam: i also noticed kernel selection changed which kernel variant we use for attention_small_seq: `attn_v2` instead of `attn_v1`. attn_v2 calls an extra transform kernel that touches prefix buffers. that transform is executed on a separate stream to overlap compute, but that breaks our cache access pattern.

Elaine: simple short-term mitigation: force the transform to run on the same stream for now or coalesce the transform into the attention kernel path. long-term: ensure KV cache keys are independent of ephemeral stream ids and add a unit/integration test that asserts prefix reuse across ramps.

Mike: i can do the canary: revert stream assignment for that transform and run a smoke profile across our canary cluster. will post numbers in ~30m. :thumbsup:

Sam: thanks. after a quick local patch (run transform on same stream) KV hit rate rose to ~88% and p99 dropped back to ~72ms. pushing a PR with test.

Elaine: please tag me in the PR and add the nsys trace as an artifact. also open a follow-up to add a perf regression test in CI that fails if KV hit rate drops >10% for small-seq workloads.

Mike: noted. i'll run extended sweeps tonight to validate memory pressure corners.

Sam: attaching the minimal repro command: `python tools/repro_kv_regress.py --seed 42 --requests 200 --seq 12 --heuristic choose_small_seq_kernels --trace out.nsight`. use `scripts/kv-stats.py out.nsight` to get the KV summary.

Javier: minor nit: also capture `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(..., cudaStreamNonBlocking)` calls; nonblocking streams change ordering assumptions. did you use those?

Sam: yes, the transform used non-blocking to overlap. switching to the default stream fixed the ordering issue in the repro. i'll update PR notes.

perf-bot: regression ticket created: INF-2148 (linked to PR 4820).

Elaine: great catch. once PR lands let's run a full regression matrix (seq distribution, batch sizes, dedicated vs hosted) before marking as closed.

Sam: will do, thanks all :heart:
